langFeatures.name: Tone
langFeatures.description: Pitch changes a word's meaning.

langFeatures.name: Click consonants
langFeatures.description: Clicks used as ordinary consonants.

langFeatures.name: Noun classes
langFeatures.description: Nouns sorted into many classes that trigger agreement across the sentence.

langFeatures.name: Evidentiality
langFeatures.description: Grammar marks how you know something — seen, heard, inferred.

langFeatures.name: Ergativity
langFeatures.description: The subject of a transitive verb is marked differently from other subjects.
langFeatures.examples: Basque, Georgian, Mayan languages, Inuktitut, Warlpiri

langFeatures.name: Polysynthesis
langFeatures.description: Whole sentences packed into one long word.

langFeatures.name: Vowel harmony
langFeatures.description: Vowels in a word must match in quality.

langFeatures.name: Honorific registers
langFeatures.description: Different words or forms depending on social status.

langFeatures.name: Inclusive / exclusive ‘we’
langFeatures.description: Separate words for ‘we including you’ and ‘we excluding you’.
langFeatures.examples: Tagalog, Malay, Quechua, Tok Pisin, Cherokee

langFeatures.name: Absolute direction
langFeatures.description: Cardinal or landscape directions instead of left/right.

langFeatures.name: Avoidance speech
langFeatures.description: Special vocabulary used around certain relatives.

langFeatures.name: Whistled speech
langFeatures.description: Speech carried as whistles across distance.
langFeatures.examples: Silbo Gomero, Kuşköy Turkish, Mazatec, Hmong

langFeatures.name: Drummed speech
langFeatures.description: Tones reproduced on talking drums.

langFeatures.name: Non-decimal counting
langFeatures.description: Counting in base 20, base 12, or by body parts.

langFeatures.name: Classifiers
langFeatures.description: Counting words that sort things by shape or kind.

langFeatures.name: Reduplication
langFeatures.description: Repeating words or syllables for plural, intensity or meaning.

langFeatures.name: Verb-initial order
langFeatures.description: Sentences start with the verb (VSO / VOS).

langFeatures.name: Ideophones
langFeatures.description: Vivid sound-symbolic words for sensations.

langFeatures.name: Animacy
langFeatures.description: Grammar distinguishes animate from inanimate.

langFeatures.name: Secret or ritual register
langFeatures.description: A special speech form for initiates or ritual.

langFeatures.name: Mixed / contact language
langFeatures.description: Born from contact between peoples.
langFeatures.examples: Michif, Tok Pisin, Haitian Creole, Chavacano

langFeatures.name: Diglossia
langFeatures.description: A ‘high’ written form and a ‘low’ spoken form coexist.

langFeatures.name: Unusual time metaphors
langFeatures.description: Past ahead and future behind, or other mappings.

langFeatures.name: Huge consonant inventory
langFeatures.description: Dozens of consonants (or very few).

writingSystems.name: Latin alphabet
writingSystems.used: Most of Europe, the Americas, Africa, Oceania

writingSystems.name: Cyrillic
writingSystems.used: Slavic, Central Asian and Caucasian languages

writingSystems.name: Arabic script
writingSystems.used: Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Pashto, Uyghur, Ajami for African languages

writingSystems.name: Chinese characters (Hanzi / Kanji / Hanja)
writingSystems.used: Chinese, Japanese, historically Korean and Vietnamese

languageFamilies.name: Niger-Congo (incl. Bantu)
languageFamilies.note: The world's largest family by number of languages.

languageFamilies.name: Afroasiatic
languageFamilies.note: Semitic, Berber, Cushitic, Chadic, Omotic and Egyptian branches.

languages.name: Arabic (Egyptian, Levantine, Maghrebi, Gulf, Hassaniya and more)

languageFamilies.name: Nilo-Saharan (proposed)
languageFamilies.note: A debated grouping of Saharan and Nilotic languages.

languageFamilies.name: Khoe and San languages (several families)
languageFamilies.note: ‘Khoisan’ is a convenience label, not a proven family.

languageFamilies.name: Indo-European
languageFamilies.note: Spread from the Pontic steppe across Eurasia, then globally through colonialism.

languageFamilies.name: Uralic
languageFamilies.note: Finnic, Sámi, Hungarian and Siberian branches.

languageFamilies.name: Turkic
languageFamilies.note: From Anatolia to Siberia.

languageFamilies.name: Sino-Tibetan
languageFamilies.note: Sinitic and Tibeto-Burman branches.

languageFamilies.name: Japonic & Koreanic
languageFamilies.note: Two small families, often grouped regionally.

languageFamilies.name: Austronesian
languageFamilies.note: Spread by voyaging from Taiwan to Madagascar and Rapa Nui.

languageFamilies.name: Kartvelian & North Caucasian families
languageFamilies.note: Three separate families with famously rich consonant systems.

languageFamilies.name: Salishan & Wakashan
languageFamilies.note: Pacific Northwest families.

languageFamilies.name: Oto-Manguean
languageFamilies.note: Highly tonal languages of Mexico.

languageFamilies.name: South American families
languageFamilies.note: Quechuan, Aymaran, Tupian, Arawakan, Cariban and many more.

languageFamilies.name: Australian languages (Pama-Nyungan and others)
languageFamilies.note: Around 250 languages at colonisation; many now revitalising.

languageFamilies.name: Papuan & Melanesian
languageFamilies.note: Hundreds of languages in dozens of families on and around New Guinea.

languageFamilies.name: Creoles & contact languages
languageFamilies.note: New languages born from contact, often in colonial violence and resistance.

languageFamilies.name: Isolates & lost languages
languageFamilies.note: Languages with no proven relatives.

languageFamilies.name: Sign languages
languageFamilies.note: Full languages with their own grammar — not signed versions of spoken languages.

languageFamilies.name: Constructed & ritual languages (real)
languageFamilies.note: Real-world precedents for invented and sacred languages.
